text:
[title] Result: 2.4x more requests per second
[body] Same hardware: 8 GPUs, same latency target
[body] Median response time unchanged
[body] Measured on a real chat workload

novice.takeaway: The presenter is showing that their method achieved 2.4x more requests per second on the same hardware without hurting response times, tested on real chat data.
questions: What exactly counts as a 'request' here?
How was 'latency target' defined or measured?
What was the actual workload size or scale tested?
novice.inferred_claim: The presenter wants us to believe their optimization technique meaningfully improves real-world serving efficiency.

peer.takeaway: The presented optimizations achieved 2.4x higher throughput on the same hardware without degrading median latency, validated on real chat traffic.
questions: What is the actual latency target value used?
How is 'requests per second' measured exactly?
peer.inferred_claim: The presenter wants us to believe their combined techniques deliver a substantial, validated throughput gain at no latency cost.

expert.takeaway: The presenter reports a 2.4x throughput gain over the same hardware and latency target, validated on a real chat workload, but the metric shifts from earlier p99 goodput to plain requests/sec.
questions: Is this 2.4x the same metric as the p99 goodput claim in slide 1?
Why report median instead of p99 if tail latency was the original motivation?
What is the actual req/s baseline vs improved number?
expert.inferred_claim: The system doubles-plus throughput without sacrificing latency, on realistic workloads.

slide_intent.text: Achieving 2.4x throughput improvement while meeting latency targets on real chat workloads demonstrates substantial performance gains.
